newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil sees Unibanco depositary pricing in 2 weeks.
newsitem.headline: Brazil sees Unibanco depositary pricing in 2 weeks.

text.p: Brazil's Central Bank said Wednesday it hoped to price its upcoming offer of global depositary shares in Brazilian bank Unibanco in the week starting May 19.

The Central Bank will sell prefered shares in Unibanco and shares in the holding that controls the bank as part of a program to clear up the debts of failed bank Banco Nacional, Central Bank international affairs director Gustavo Franco said.
Unibanco deposited shares worth about 682 million reais with the Central Bank as part of a "goodwill" payment made during its buyout of the healthy assets of Nacional.
The shares have since doubled in value to around 1.2 billion reais although that value was "theoretic" because shares in the Unibanco holding are not publicly traded, Franco said.
However, given that the holding's only asset is Unibanco, its shares were worth the same as the bank's and the two types would be sold together in units during the depositary receipt offer, he said.
Receipts from the sale would be used by the Central Bank to pay off Banco Nacional's negative assets which it took on at the time of its takeover by Unibanco.
Morgan Stanley & Co., J.P. Morgan & Co., Lehman Bros. and SBC Warburg Inc. would coordinate the U.S. and other international tranches of the offer, Franco said.
